children.title: Stage A: eigen-relation and uniform lost count for re-attachments of a normal-form counterexample
children.statement_en: Let n >= 3, d a natural number, and G a graph on Fin n in normal form NF(d): every degree is d or d + 1, and vertices of equal degree have isomorphic cards; let H be hypomorphic to G and not isomorphic to G (a counterexample pair). Write K for the family of labelled graphs on Fin n hypomorphic to G; K, K' agree off u if they have the same adjacency on every pair avoiding u; the re-attachment class C_G(u) is the set of members of K agreeing with G off u. Then (a) every K in K has all degrees d or d + 1 (A0); (b) for every K in K and every u there is K' != K in K agreeing with K off u (A3, re-attachment); (c) there is an integer theta such that for all K1, K2 in K agreeing off u, with z(y) = [K1.Adj u y] - [K2.Adj u y] (integers): deg_K1 x = deg_K2 x + z(x) for every x (A2(a)), and for every x != u, sum over K1-neighbours y of x of z(y) equals (theta - s) z(x), where s = 1 if u has degree d + 1 in K1 and 0 otherwise (A2(c), Zinchenko arXiv:2611.13728 Lemma 3.1(c)); (d) for every K in K and K1, K2 in K agreeing with K off u, both different from K, the number of K-neighbours of u lost in K1 equals the number lost in K2, and K1.Adj u x <-> K2.Adj u x for every x with deg_K x = deg_K u (A5 = Lemma 3.4 / Cor 3.5(a)). See debe_zinchenko.md section 4, Stage A.
children.statement_lean: ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → ∀ (d : ℕ) (G H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), (∀ x : Fin n, (G.neighborSet x).ncard = d ∨ (G.neighborSet x).ncard = d + 1) → (∀ x y : Fin n, (G.neighborSet x).ncard = (G.neighborSet y).ncard → Nonempty (G.induce ({x}ᶜ : Set (Fin n)) ≃g G.induce ({y}ᶜ : Set (Fin n)))) → Recon.Hypomorphic G H → ¬ Nonempty (G ≃g H) → let dg := fun (K : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (x : Fin n) => (K.neighborSet x).ncard; let ag := fun (A B : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (u : Fin n) => ∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ u → y ≠ u → (A.Adj x y ↔ B.Adj x y); let z := fun (A B : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (u y : Fin n) => (Set.indicator {w : Fin n | A.Adj u w} 1 y : ℤ) - Set.indicator {w : Fin n | B.Adj u w} 1 y; (∀ K : SimpleGraph (Fin n), Recon.Hypomorphic G K → ∀ x : Fin n, dg K x = d ∨ dg K x = d + 1) ∧ (∀ K : SimpleGraph (Fin n), Recon.Hypomorphic G K → ∀ u : Fin n, ∃ K' : SimpleGraph (Fin n), Recon.Hypomorphic G K' ∧ ag K K' u ∧ K' ≠ K) ∧ ∃ θ : ℤ, (∀ K₁ K₂ : SimpleGraph (Fin n), Recon.Hypomorphic G K₁ → Recon.Hypomorphic G K₂ → ∀ u : Fin n, ag K₁ K₂ u → ∀ x : Fin n, (dg K₁ x : ℤ) = dg K₂ x + z K₁ K₂ u x ∧ (x ≠ u → ∑ y : Fin n, Set.indicator {w : Fin n | K₁.Adj x w} (z K₁ K₂ u) y = (θ - (if dg K₁ u = d + 1 then 1 else 0)) * z K₁ K₂ u x)) ∧ ∀ K K₁ K₂ : SimpleGraph (Fin n), Recon.Hypomorphic G K → Recon.Hypomorphic G K₁ → Recon.Hypomorphic G K₂ → ∀ u : Fin n, ag K K₁ u → ag K K₂ u → K₁ ≠ K → K₂ ≠ K → Set.ncard {y : Fin n | K.Adj u y ∧ ¬ K₁.Adj u y} = Set.ncard {y : Fin n | K.Adj u y ∧ ¬ K₂.Adj u y} ∧ ∀ x : Fin n, dg K x = dg K u → (K₁.Adj u x ↔ K₂.Adj u x)

children.title: Stage B low case: given Stage A, a low vertex of a normal-form counterexample has at most two re-attachments
children.statement_en: Let n >= 3, d a natural number, and G a graph on Fin n in normal form NF(d): every degree is d or d + 1, and vertices of equal degree have isomorphic cards; let H be hypomorphic to G and not isomorphic to G (a counterexample pair). Write K for the family of labelled graphs on Fin n hypomorphic to G; K, K' agree off u if they have the same adjacency on every pair avoiding u; the re-attachment class C_G(u) is the set of members of K agreeing with G off u. Assume the Stage A conclusions (a)-(d) of the sibling extension_eigen hold for G (stated verbatim as a hypothesis, with the same let-abbreviations dg, ag, z). Then, for every vertex u of degree d (low) and any three members K1, K2, K3 of C_G(u), two of them are equal, i.e. |C_G(u)| <= 2 (Zinchenko Thm 4.4, low case; debe_zinchenko.md section 4, B1-B4, with A6 transport left to the builder).

children.title: Complement transfer: the low-vertex bound on re-attachment classes gives the bound at every vertex
children.statement_en: Assume: for every normal-form counterexample (n >= 3, NF(d), G hypomorphic to H, G not isomorphic to H), every vertex u of degree d and any three members of C_G(u), two are equal. Then the same conclusion holds for every vertex u, without the degree condition (Zinchenko Thm 4.4 high case via the complement, Lemma 2.5: a high vertex of G is low in the complement, which is in NF(n - 2 - d) with the complementary counterexample partner, and C of the complement is the complement of C; debe_zinchenko.md B5).

children.title: A non-extending card isomorphism plus a non-isomorphic hypomorphic partner yields three re-attachments
children.statement_en: Let n >= 3, G and H graphs on Fin n with G hypomorphic to H and not isomorphic to H, alpha : G - u -> G - u' a card isomorphism and x a neighbour of u with alpha(x) not adjacent to u'. Then there are three pairwise distinct graphs K1, K2, K3, each hypomorphic to G and each agreeing with G on every pair avoiding u': G itself, the graph obtained from G - u' by re-attaching u' to alpha(N(u)) (isomorphic to G, different from G at the pair u', alpha(x)), and the re-attachment of u' along a card isomorphism G - u' -> H - sigma(u') (isomorphic to H). debe_zinchenko.md section 6, paper argument for N.
